## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Boldteq Marketing Site — 500+ Bug Deep-Dive Audit Prompt

## Context
Webflow→Next.js 16 marketing site at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq. 21 routes, 212 src files, 33,001-line Webflow CSS reference, CMS CSVs, Playwright wired. Live ref: https://boldteq.com. Goal: surface 500+ defects across visual / responsive / interactive / a11y / SEO / perf / type-safety / content / SEO / build dimensions, organized into fix batches. This file is the **prompt** that the next-phase audit agent will run. No code changes happen here — only plan + prompt.

## Why now
Site rebuilt page-by-page over many sessions. Drift accumulated: Tailwind-defaults snuck in instead of exact Webflow values, responsive breakpoints missed, a11y not gated, SEO partial, no consolidated bug ledger. Need single sweep producing actionable ledger before fixing.

## Phase 1 deliverable (this plan)
The audit prompt below. Phase 2 = run prompt (multi-agent, parallel by route + dimension), produces `audit/bugs.json` ledger. Phase 3 = batched fixes in priority order.

---

## THE DEEP-DIVE AUDIT PROMPT (verbatim — paste to dispatcher next phase)

> ### Mission
> Find and document 500+ defects across the Boldteq marketing site (`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq`). Output a structured bug ledger at `audit/bugs.json` + Markdown summary at `audit/REPORT.md`. Do NOT fix anything. Audit only.
>
> ### Sources of truth (strict priority)
> 1. Live site → https://boldteq.com (Playwright screenshots @ 1440 / 1280 / 991 / 767 / 479)
> 2. Webflow HTML → `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/*.html` (markup, classnames, content, structure)
> 3. Webflow CSS → `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css` (33,001 lines, exact values)
> 4. CMS CSVs → `CMS Data/*.csv` (portfolio×21, blog×6, blog-cat×6, portfolio-cat×8)
> 5. Project CLAUDE.md → constraints, design system, page map
>
> ### Routes in scope (21)
> `/`, `/pricing`, `/our-works`, `/our-works/[slug]` (×9: dabble, cinea, dog-crate, junoone, better-days, lippy-oil, frames-for-prints, repower-electric-supply, sandscents), `/how-it-works`, `/contact`, `/beta`, `/careers`, `/blog`, `/blog/[slug]` (×6), `/our-mission`, `/book-a-demo`, `/scope`, `/testimonials`, `/privacy-policy`, `/terms-of-service`, `/newsletter`, `/services/website-development`, `/services/ui-ux-design`, `/services/graphics-design`, `/services/app-development`. Plus shared: navbar, footer, beta-cta, newsletter-signup, cta-banner.
>
> ### Audit dimensions (14) — every route × every dimension
>
> **D1. Visual fidelity vs live + Webflow**
> - Section count / order matches
> - Typography: font-family Roobert PRO loaded (4 weights 300/400/500/700), font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, weight per heading + body within ±1px
> - Colors exact: #092245, #082753, #21cfff, #019ae6, gradients, #f5f7fa, badge greens/oranges
> - Spacing: padding, margin, gap exact from Webflow CSS — no Tailwind-default substitutions
> - Border-radius (10/15/20/999), box-shadow values exact
> - Image dimensions, aspect ratio, object-fit, container max-width (1280 / 1300 portfolio)
>
> **D2. Responsive — 5 breakpoints**
> - 1440+, 1280+, 991-, 767-, 479-
> - Layout shifts, container widths, grid column counts, font scaling, hidden/shown elements per breakpoint
> - Compare each breakpoint vs Webflow CSS @media rules + live screenshots
>
> **D3. Interactive states**
> - hover / focus / active / disabled / visited for every link, button, card, input
> - Cursor states correct (pointer/text/not-allowed)
> - Transitions / animations match (duration, easing, transform origin)
>
> **D4. Forms**
> - Contact form: 6 fields (First/Last/Email/Phone/Looking-for-dropdown with 5 options/Message) — Zod validation, required attrs, success message exact text
> - Newsletter signup (footer + standalone page) — email validation, success/error states
> - Beta page form — fields + submit
> - Book-a-demo Calendly embed loads
> - Field labels, placeholders, error text, success text from Webflow exactly
>
> **D5. Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)**
> - Heading hierarchy h1→h2→h3 (single h1 per route)
> - Alt text on every image (descriptive, not filename)
> - Color contrast ratios ≥4.5:1 body, ≥3:1 large text
> - Keyboard navigation: tab order, focus rings visible, skip-to-content
> - ARIA: role, aria-label, aria-expanded on dropdowns/accordions/sheets, aria-current on nav
> - Form labels associated (htmlFor/id), error messages aria-describedby
> - Modal focus trap + Escape close + return focus
> - Decorative SVGs aria-hidden
>
> **D6. SEO**
> - Per-route unique `<title>` ≤60 chars, meta description ≤160 chars, canonical URL
> - Open Graph: og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630), og:url, og:type
> - Twitter card tags
> - JSON-LD: Organization (all routes), FAQPage (`/`), Service+Offers (`/pricing`), BreadcrumbList (case studies + blog), Article (blog posts), BlogPosting
> - Sitemap.xml includes all 21 routes + 9 case studies + 6 blog posts
> - robots.ts allows production, disallows previews
> - Google verification meta `JlE0J7GQIyTbyMqTli7Z0EOoLHC08lyX-cdkTY9iRLI`
> - metadataBase = https://boldteq.com
> - Internal links use Next `<Link>`, not `<a>` (except external)
> - Image alt text descriptive
>
> **D7. Performance**
> - LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, INP <200ms — measure via Lighthouse
> - Above-fold images: `priority`, `loading="eager"`, correct `sizes`
> - Below-fold images: `loading="lazy"`
> - Font-display swap, preload critical Roobert PRO weights
> - No layout shift from font swap (size-adjust)
> - JS bundle per route — flag any route >200kb gzip
> - Embla / Framer Motion lazy-loaded where possible
> - Image format: WebP/AVIF, not raw PNG/JPG where Webflow CDN serves both
>
> **D8. TypeScript strict**
> - Zero `any` (grep `: any\b`, `as any`, `<any>`)
> - Zero `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` without justification comment
> - All component props typed via interface, no inline anonymous types in exported components
> - Constants in `src/lib/constants/*` typed via interfaces from `src/types/*`
>
> **D9. Build / lint**
> - `pnpm build` — must pass with 0 errors, 0 warnings
> - `pnpm lint` — must pass clean
> - No unused imports, vars, files
> - No `console.log`, `console.warn`, `debugger` in src
> - No TODO/FIXME without ticket reference
>
> **D10. Runtime / hydration**
> - Open every route in dev — flag every console error / warning
> - Hydration mismatches (SSR ≠ client)
> - Client components correctly marked `"use client"`
> - Server components don't import client-only libs
> - Image src never undefined / empty
> - Links never `href=""` or `href="#"` (unless intentional)
>
> **D11. Routing / boundaries**
> - 404 page exists + branded
> - Global error.tsx + per-route error.tsx where async
> - Loading.tsx for slow routes
> - Dynamic routes [slug]: generateStaticParams covers all CMS items, notFound() for unknown slug
> - Trailing slash consistency
> - No broken internal links (crawl all `<Link href>` + `<a href>`)
>
> **D12. Page-specific content match (vs Webflow HTML)**
> - **Home** — 13 sections: Trustpilot badge, typewriter (3 phrases exact: "Ownership Driven", "Without Hiring", "On Demand"), h2-then-h1, 3 trust badges, GuideJar embed, dual CTAs, infinite logo scroll, portfolio carousel 4 cats, 3 pain points, resolution banner with team img, 4 numbered stages, 6-card benefits grid, 3-step how-it-works, pricing toggle (3 plans $999/$1999/$3499), comparison table, 8-item FAQ
> - **Pricing** — pricing section reused + Custom Plan CTA + ROI calculator (presets Startup/Growth/Enterprise, sliders, animated counters)
> - **Our Works** — hero + 4 trust badges, filter header, 305px sidebar + 2col grid (1fr 1fr), card image-only with 280/400/450 heights, category badge, eye icon, popup modal (iframe vs gallery), 8/page pagination 44px buttons, Shopify+WordPress active + 5 Coming Soon
> - **Case studies (9)** — slug match, hero, gallery, related works
> - **How It Works** — hero+4 stat badges + GuideJar, 3col agency-fit, 3-step screenshots, 4-step workflow, "Designed to Remove Risk" 4 cards
> - **Contact** — 3 info cards (sales@/support@/hr@), full form, success exact text "Thank you! Your submission has been received! Our team will get back to you within 12-24hrs."
> - **Beta** — beta-only pricing $299 / $599, bug report card, add-on hours, 3-step how-it-works, 3-segment "who it's built for", final CTA "Your Execution Team. Live in 12 Hours."
> - **Careers** — 4-step selection, tabs (About/Culture/Benefits/Opportunities), 5 job listings, benchmarks, 4 team testimonials, global impact
> - **Blog** — listing with category filter, 6 posts, post detail with HTML content from CSV
> - **Our Mission** — full content vs our-mission.html
> - **Book a Demo** — Calendly + supporting copy
> - **Scope** — 4 platform tabs (Shopify / WordPress / Shopify Apps / Frontend) × 4 tier tabs (Small/Medium/Large/Support) — every card content vs scope.html
> - **Testimonials** — every quote vs testimonials.html
> - **Privacy / Terms / Newsletter** — body copy exact
> - **Services** — website-development full + 3 coming-soon shells matching Webflow
>
> **D13. Shared components**
> - **Navbar** — sticky trigger 300px desktop / 350px mobile, Solutions dropdown (Web Dev link + 3 Coming Soon), "View Full Service Scope" link, Resources dropdown (Blog + help.boldteq.com), Login (portal.boldteq.com) + Schedule Demo CTAs, mobile sheet 300px #082753
> - **Footer** — newsletter card + 4 link cols (About/Services/Resources/Help), Coming Soon badges, logo + LinkedIn/IG/FB icons, "Designed with ❤️ from India 🇮🇳"
> - **Beta CTA** — bottom of most pages: 🔒 Exclusive + 4 checkmarks, Founding Partner Pricing + 15-agency urgency, modal close (✕ / Esc / overlay)
> - **Newsletter signup** — email + submit + privacy line above BetaCta
> - **CTA banner** — navy bg, padding 40px 20px 50px, default "Ready to Deliver This Level of Work Under Your Brand?"
>
> **D14. CMS data integrity**
> - Portfolio: all 21 CSV rows surface in `/our-works` (sort by `order`), images load, slugs map to detail pages, categories match
> - Blog: 6 posts surface, categories filter works, HTML content renders sanitized
> - Categories: 8 portfolio + 6 blog all reachable
>
> ### Tooling — required commands
> ```bash
> pnpm build                           # D9
> pnpm lint                            # D9
> grep -rn ": any\b\|as any\|@ts-ignore\|@ts-expect-error\|console\.\(log\|warn\)\|debugger" src
> pnpm exec playwright test            # D1, D2, D10
> pnpm exec next-sitemap                # D6
> npx @lhci/cli autorun                # D7 (Lighthouse)
> npx pa11y-ci <route>                 # D5 (a11y)
> ```
>
> Playwright spec must screenshot live + local @ 5 breakpoints × 21 routes (210 screenshots), diff via pixelmatch, flag any region >2% delta. Use existing tests/ scaffolding.
>
> ### Output format — `audit/bugs.json`
> ```json
> [
>   {
>     "id": "BT-0001",
>     "dimension": "D1",
>     "severity": "P0|P1|P2|P3",
>     "route": "/",
>     "component": "src/components/home/hero.tsx",
>     "line": 42,
>     "title": "Hero h1 font-size 48px, Webflow spec 50px",
>     "evidence": "boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css:1234 → 3.125rem; src/components/home/hero.module.css:18 → 3rem",
>     "live_screenshot": "audit/screens/live-home-hero-1440.png",
>     "local_screenshot": "audit/screens/local-home-hero-1440.png",
>     "fix_hint": "Change .heroH1 font-size to 3.125rem",
>     "estimated_minutes": 2,
>     "blocks": []
>   }
> ]
> ```
>
> Severity rules:
> - P0 — broken / unusable / form fails / build error / route 404s
> - P1 — visible visual mismatch above fold / a11y violation / SEO miss on key route
> - P2 — below-fold visual / minor a11y / typed `any`
> - P3 — polish / micro-spacing
>
> ### Output format — `audit/REPORT.md`
> - Executive summary: total bug count by dimension × severity
> - Top 20 P0/P1
> - Per-route bug count
> - Recommended fix batches (group by file/component for parallel fixing)
>
> ### Acceptance — phase 2 complete when
> - ≥500 bugs logged across 14 dimensions, ≥10 per route avg
> - Every bug has: id, dimension, severity, route, component, evidence, fix_hint
> - Screenshots committed to `audit/screens/`
> - REPORT.md groups bugs into fix batches sized for 1-hour parallel sessions
> - Build still passes (no audit code in src/)

---

## Critical files to read before running prompt

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) — page map, design system, rules
- [boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css](boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css) — 33k lines exact CSS
- [src/app/layout.tsx](src/app/layout.tsx), [src/app/globals.css](src/app/globals.css) — root chrome
- [src/lib/seo/metadata.ts](src/lib/seo/metadata.ts), [src/lib/seo/jsonld.tsx](src/lib/seo/jsonld.tsx) — SEO utilities
- [src/lib/constants/](src/lib/constants/) — extracted data
- [tests/](tests/) — existing Playwright + audit scripts (reuse, don't duplicate)
- [next.config.ts](next.config.ts) — image domains, redirects

## Verification (how to know prompt produced correct ledger)

1. `cat audit/bugs.json | jq 'length'` ≥ 500
2. `cat audit/bugs.json | jq 'group_by(.dimension) | map({dim: .[0].dimension, n: length})'` — all 14 dimensions hit
3. `cat audit/bugs.json | jq 'group_by(.route) | map({route: .[0].route, n: length})'` — every route ≥10
4. Spot-check 10 random P0/P1 — open file at line, confirm bug real
5. `audit/screens/` has live + local pair per breakpoint per route

## Phase 3 preview (after ledger ready — not part of this plan)

- Group bugs by component file → parallel fix batches
- One agent per batch, 1-hour TTL
- Re-run audit after each batch, expect bug count to drop
- Final pass: full Playwright + Lighthouse + pa11y green

---

## Open questions for Yash before running phase 2

1. Run audit headless or live-watch?
2. Cap Lighthouse to mobile-only or both mobile+desktop?
3. Include Sentry/PostHog wiring audit (env-dependent) or skip?
4. Live site is single source of truth when it conflicts with Webflow HTML — confirm?

# Boldteq Marketing Site — 500+ Bug Deep-Dive Audit Prompt

## Context
Webflow→Next.js 16 marketing site at /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq. 21 routes, 212 src files, 33,001-line Webflow CSS reference, CMS CSVs, Playwright wired. Live ref: https://boldteq.com. Goal: surface 500+ defects across visual / responsive / interactive / a11y / SEO / perf / type-safety / content / SEO / build dimensions, organized into fix batches. This file is the **prompt** that the next-phase audit agent will run. No code changes happen here — only plan + prompt.

## Why now
Site rebuilt page-by-page over many sessions. Drift accumulated: Tailwind-defaults snuck in instead of exact Webflow values, responsive breakpoints missed, a11y not gated, SEO partial, no consolidated bug ledger. Need single sweep producing actionable ledger before fixing.

## Phase 1 deliverable (this plan)
The audit prompt below. Phase 2 = run prompt (multi-agent, parallel by route + dimension), produces `audit/bugs.json` ledger. Phase 3 = batched fixes in priority order.

---

## THE DEEP-DIVE AUDIT PROMPT (verbatim — paste to dispatcher next phase)

> ### Mission
> Find and document 500+ defects across the Boldteq marketing site (`/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Marketing Site/Boldteq`). Output a structured bug ledger at `audit/bugs.json` + Markdown summary at `audit/REPORT.md`. Do NOT fix anything. Audit only.
>
> ### Sources of truth (strict priority)
> 1. Live site → https://boldteq.com (Playwright screenshots @ 1440 / 1280 / 991 / 767 / 479)
> 2. Webflow HTML → `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/*.html` (markup, classnames, content, structure)
> 3. Webflow CSS → `boldteq-v1-0.webflow/css/boldteq-v1-0.webflow.css` (33,001 lines, exact values)
> 4. CMS CSVs → `CMS Data/*.csv` (portfolio×21, blog×6, blog-cat×6, portfolio-cat×8)
> 5. Project CLAUDE.md → constraints, design system, page map
>
> ### Routes in scope (21)
> `/`, `/pricing`, `/our-works`, `/our-works/[slug]` (×9: dabble, cinea, dog-crate, junoone, better-days, lippy-oil, frames-for-prints, repower-electric-supply, sandscents), `/how-it-works`, `/contact`, `/beta`, `/careers`, `/blog`, `/blog/[slug]` (×6), `/our-mission`, `/book-a-demo`, `/scope`, `/testimonials`, `/privacy-policy`, `/terms-of-service`, `/newsletter`, `/services/website-development`, `/services/ui-ux-design`, `/services/graphics-design`, `/services/app-development`. Plus shared: navbar, footer, beta-cta, newsletter-signup, cta-banner.
>
> ### Audit dimensions (14) — every route × every dimension
>
> **D1. Visual fidelity vs live + Webflow**
> - Section count / order matches
> - Typography: font-family Roobert PRO loaded (4 weights 300/400/500/700), font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, weight per heading + body within ±1px
> - Colors exact: #092245, #082753, #21cfff, #019ae6, gradients, #f5f7fa, badge greens/oranges
> - Spacing: padding, margin, gap exact from Webflow CSS — no Tailwind-default substitutions
> - Border-radius (10/15/20/999), box-shadow values exact
> - Image dimensions, aspect ratio, object-fit, container max-width (1280 / 1300 portfolio)
>
> **D2. Responsive — 5 breakpoints**
> - 1440+, 1280+, 991-, 767-, 479-
> - Layout shifts, container widths, grid column counts, font scaling, hidden/shown elements per breakpoint
> - Compare each breakpoint vs Webflow CSS @media rules + live screenshots
>
> **D3. Interactive states**
> - hover / focus / active / disabled / visited for every link, button, card, input
> - Cursor states correct (pointer/text/not-allowed)
> - Transitions / animations match (duration, easing, transform origin)
>
> **D4. Forms**
> - Contact form: 6 fields (First/Last/Email/Phone/Looking-for-dropdown with 5 options/Message) — Zod validation, required attrs, success message exact text
> - Newsletter signup (footer + standalone page) — email validation, success/error states
> - Beta page form — fields + submit
> - Book-a-demo Calendly embed loads
> - Field labels, placeholders, error text, success text from Webflow exactly
>
> **D5. Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)**
> - Heading hierarchy h1→h2→h3 (single h1 per route)
> - Alt text on every image (descriptive, not filename)
> - Color contrast ratios ≥4.5:1 body, ≥3:1 large text
> - Keyboard navigation: tab order, focus rings visible, skip-to-content
> - ARIA: role, aria-label, aria-expanded on dropdowns/accordions/sheets, aria-current on nav
> - Form labels associated (htmlFor/id), error messages aria-describedby
> - Modal focus trap + Escape close + return focus
> - Decorative SVGs aria-hidden
>
> **D6. SEO**
> - Per-route unique `<title>` ≤60 chars, meta description ≤160 chars, canonical URL
> - Open Graph: og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630), og:url, og:type
> - Twitter card tags
> - JSON-LD: Organization (all routes), FAQPage (`/`), Service+Offers (`/pricing`), BreadcrumbList (case studies + blog), Article (blog posts), BlogPosting
> - Sitemap.xml includes all 21 routes + 9 case studies + 6 blog posts
> - robots.ts allows production, disallows previews
> - Google verification meta `JlE0J7GQIyTbyMqTli7Z0EOoLHC08lyX-cdkTY9iRLI`
> - metadataBase = https://boldteq.com
> - Internal links use Next `<Link>`, not `<a>` (except external)
> - Image alt text descriptive
>
> **D7. Performance**
> - LCP <2.5s, CLS <0.1, INP <200ms — measure via Lighthouse
> - Above-fold images: `priority`, `loading="eager"`, correct `sizes`
> - Below-fold images: `loading="lazy"`
> - Font-display swap, preload critical Roobert PRO weights
> - No layout shift from font swap (size-adjust)
> - JS bundle per route — flag any route >200kb gzip
> - Embla / Framer Motion lazy-loaded where possible
> - Image format: WebP/AVIF, not raw PNG/JPG where Webflow CDN serves both
>
> **D8. TypeScript strict**
> - Zero `any` (grep `: any\b`, `as any`, `<any>`)
> - Zero `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` without justification comment
> - All component props typed via interface, no inline anonymous types in exported components
> - Constants in `src/lib/constants/*` typed via interfaces from `src/types/*`
>
> **D9. Build / lint**
> - `pnpm build` — must pass with 0 errors, 0 warnings
> - `pnpm lint` — must pass clean
> - No unused imports, vars, files
> - No `console.log`, `console.warn`, `debugger` in src
> - No TODO/FIXME without ticket reference
>
> **D10. Runtime / hydration**
> - Open every route in dev — flag every console error / warning
> - Hydration mismatches (SSR ≠ client)
> - Client components correctly marked `"use client"`
> - Server components don't import client-only libs
> - Image src never undefined / empty
> - Links never `href=""` or `href="#"` (unless intentional)
>
> **D11. Routing / boundaries**
> - 404 page exists + branded

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- caveman:caveman-commit: Ultra-compressed commit message generator. Cuts noise from commit messages while preserving intent and reasoning. Conventional Commits format. Subject ≤50 chars, body only when "why" isn't obvious. Use when user says "write a commit", "commit message", "generate commit", "/commit", or invokes /caveman-commit. Auto-triggers when staging changes.
- caveman:caveman: Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts token usage ~75% by speaking like caveman while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra, wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra. Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens", "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
- caveman:compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman:compress <filepath> or "compress memory file"
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- caveman:caveman-review: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
